title: Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks and appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages
content:
## 3.1 Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks and appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages

### Overall structure of the work plan

FIELDWISE is a single-beneficiary MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is recruited by and hosted at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (ATK) in Martonvásár, Hungary, under primary supervision by Dr. Roland Hollós (ATK) and co-supervision by Prof. András Jung at the associated partner Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE). It is a European Fellowship of 30 months: a 24-month research fellowship at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (M1-M24) followed by a six-month non-academic placement at AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság (M25-M30). There is no separate secondment; the placement is the inter-sectoral mobility element and is shown on the Gantt chart.

The work plan is organised into five work packages that follow the scientific logic of the objectives from raw evidence to operational uptake, so that each work package consumes a validated output of its predecessor rather than running in parallel silos:

- WP1 - Data Harmonisation and Physiological Stress Definition (lead: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont) delivers objective O1: it harmonises the heterogeneous 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive of Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem (MATE) into a QC-controlled common-variable matrix and fixes a physiologically meaningful water-stress target and a pre-registered validation protocol.
- WP2 - HUN-REN Modelling and ELTE Scale Harmonisation (lead: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont) delivers objective O2: it builds a parsimonious, interpretable, uncertainty-aware primary water-status model with one nonlinear benchmark where justified, separates reusable system components from crop-specific parameters, and defines the spectral/UAV/Sentinel scaling and crop-transfer specification.
- WP3 - Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation (lead: the independent commercial-farmer validation site) delivers objective O3: it instruments an independent commercial field and measures the transfer gap of the historical model prospectively, with uncertainty and any limited recalibration stated openly.
- WP4 - DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation (lead: КРУМАТИК ЕООД) delivers objective O4's build strand: it co-develops a crop-configurable DrR web MVP carrying the validated processing-tomato module and prepares the exploitation route and the placement evaluation protocol, using structured AgroVIR requirements consultation from M1.
- WP5 - AgroVIR Non-Academic Placement (lead: AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság) delivers objective O4's evaluation strand: during the M25-M30 placement it evaluates the MVP operationally within a real farm-management-information-system environment and defines the post-MSCA integration and exploitation roadmap.

The plan carries eleven deliverables and five milestones. The deliverables are: D1.1 Harmonised database/metadata and variable-availability map (M6), D1.2 Stress-target, feature-selection and validation protocol (M6), D1.3 Career Development Plan (M3); D2.1 Primary model, benchmark and model card (M14), D2.2 Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation, scaling and crop-transfer specification (M14); D3.1 Independent commercial-field validation dataset (M18), D3.2 Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (M18); D4.1 Crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (M24), D4.2 Pre-placement technical/usability requirements dossier (M24); D5.1 AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (M30), D5.2 Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (M30). The Career Development Plan (D1.3) is front-loaded to M3 so that the training and career logic frames the whole fellowship, and is reviewed at each steering point.

The five milestones are decision gates rather than restatements of deliverables, each carrying a verifiable achievement criterion: MS1 Historical knowledge base and target definition complete (M6); MS2 Model and scale-transition framework ready for final prospective assessment (M14); MS3 Independent real-world transferability quantified (M18); MS4 MVP ready for industrial placement evaluation (M24); MS5 Industrial evaluation and placement completed (M30). MS4 is the pivotal gate: only a validated, externally-access-tested MVP passes into the industrial placement, so that the M25-M30 placement is never spent stabilising an immature tool. MS5 falls in the placement's last month, so the placement window is milestoned by construction and its completion is evidenced directly by D5.1 and D5.2.

### Timing of the work packages and their components, and the critical path

The timeline fits comfortably within the 30-month duration. The confirmed schedule places WP1 in M1-M6, WP2 in M3-M14, WP3 in M4-M18, WP4 in M1-M24 and WP5 in M25-M30. Three design choices give the plan its robustness. First, WP4 runs continuously from M1 to M24: software co-development with КРУМАТИК ЕООД and AgroVIR requirements consultation (T4.4) begin at the outset rather than waiting for the science to finish, so the MVP integrates validated functions incrementally instead of in a risky end-load. Second, the field-dependent tasks of WP3 (installation T3.2 in M5-M7; coordinated physiological, proximal and thermal campaigns T3.3 in M7-M14; UAV and Sentinel acquisition T3.4 in M8-M15) are positioned to catch the growing season, and the securing of written field access (T3.1) is scheduled in M4-M6, well ahead of instrumentation. Third, the two temporally strict, finish-to-start couplings are honoured with slack: WP4 ends at M24 before WP5 starts at M25, and the migration of validated core functions (T4.3, M18-M22) precedes the placement evaluation (T5.1, M25-M27).

The critical path runs T1.3 (select the primary physiological stress target) -> T2.2 (develop the parsimonious primary model and benchmark) -> T3.5 (apply the historical model prospectively and quantify the transfer gap) -> T4.3 (migrate validated core functions toward the MVP) -> T5.1 (operational evaluation at AgroVIR). This is exactly the scientific spine of the proposal - target definition, modelling, prospective validation, productisation, industrial evaluation - which means the schedule protects the highest-value chain of work. The inter-WP dependencies are explicit: WP1 feeds WP2 and WP3 (the common-variable matrix, the stress target and the pre-registered protocol govern both), WP2 feeds WP3 (T3.5 applies the WP2 historical model prospectively) and WP4 (T4.2 implements the WP2 reusable/crop-specific separation), WP3 feeds WP4 (only the WP3-validated module migrates into D4.1), and WP4 gates WP5 through the MS4 MVP-ready check. The dependency graph is acyclic and no critical-path dependency is left unresolved.

### Appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages

The fellow's 30 person-months are distributed to match where the intellectual load lies: WP1 3.0 PM, WP2 6.0 PM, WP3 6.6 PM, WP4 6.0 PM, WP5 5.4 PM, and 3.0 PM cross-cutting (supervision cadence, training, open-science and reporting), totalling 30.0 PM. The weighting is science-heavy and honest: the two most demanding and most novel strands - modelling (WP2) and the independent prospective validation with its field campaigns (WP3) - together take almost half the fellow's time, while WP1 is deliberately lean because it reuses an existing archive rather than mounting a new data campaign. The build (WP4) and the industrial placement (WP5) are resourced enough to deliver a working MVP and a substantive operational evaluation without displacing the research core.

The fellow's effort is complemented by partner in-kind contributions that are stated as operator-declared estimates pending written partner confirmation: approximately 2.5 PM from the ATK supervisor, 2.0 PM from the ELTE co-supervisor, 3.0 PM from AgroVIR (the only partner hosting the fellow, and correspondingly the largest partner figure), 2.4 PM from MATE and 1.5 PM from КРУМАТИК ЕООД. These figures were built bottom-up from the accepted governance cadence and role descriptions and are to be verified with each partner before the grant; they are presented here as declared assumptions, not as confirmed commitments.

### Mechanisms to assess and mitigate risks

The project carries a ten-row risk register spanning research and administrative risks, each with a likelihood (L/M/H), impact (L/M/H) and a concrete mitigation, and it is anchored by an explicit risk philosophy: a drop in prospective performance is treated as a scientific result to be quantified with stated uncertainty and addressed by limited, transparent recalibration, never hidden. The register is:

- R01 Historical MATE variables differ among years (L=M, I=H): use an explicit year-by-variable matrix; harmonise only defensible common variables; retain year-specific measurements as secondary information.
- R02 Effective biological sample size is limited (L=M, I=H): use repeated-measure/hierarchical structure, conservative feature reduction and parsimonious modelling; no deep-learning dependency.
- R03 Farmer site lacks modern monitoring infrastructure (L=H, I=M): install a project meteorological station and soil sensors before the validation campaign; define maintenance and data-quality responsibilities.
- R04 Primary farmer access changes or is interrupted (L=M, I=H): secure written access; maintain the Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route as a contingency subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability.
- R05 ELTE instrument access or timing is constrained (L=M, I=H): use a written equipment/operation schedule; prioritise key physiological dates; retain physiology/proximal sensing as the core pathway if individual UAV campaigns are missed.
- R06 Field geometry or clouds limit Sentinel-2 interpretation (L=H, I=M): use Sentinel only where valid pixels support field-scale inference; rely on UAV/proximal observations for finer spatial scales.
- R07 Prospective performance drops (L=M, I=H): treat transfer loss as a scientific result; quantify uncertainty and use limited transparent recalibration rather than hiding the gap.
- R08 Krumatic web development is delayed (L=M, I=M): develop incrementally from the existing desktop prototype; scientific deliverables remain primary; prioritise validated core functions over feature breadth.
- R09 AgroVIR cannot provide proprietary/customer data (L=L, I=M): design the placement around usability/interoperability requirements and protected/coded extracts; unrestricted customer-system access is not a project dependency.
- R10 MATE-derived assets have commercial restrictions (L=M, I=H): use for approved research; maintain a background/foreground inventory and conduct an institutional data-rights/IP assessment before commercial exploitation.

The register is designed so that no single point of failure can stall the fellowship. The highest-exposure external dependencies each have a pre-planned fallback that keeps the science intact: field-site loss is covered by the Szentendre Skanzen contingency (R04, and the standing T3.6 task) and by installing the project's own meteorological and soil instrumentation (R03), so the validation does not rely on pre-existing farm infrastructure; the UAV and hyperspectral campaigns run with ELTE's instruments under a written equipment schedule, and if individual flights are missed the physiology and proximal-sensing pathway remains the core route (R05, R06); software slippage is de-risked by incremental development from the existing prototype while scientific deliverables stay primary (R08); and the placement is deliberately architected to need no proprietary or customer-data access, relying on protected, coded extracts (R09), which is why its likelihood/impact is the lowest in the table. The parsimony discipline (R01, R02) directly answers the small-sample, heterogeneous-archive reality of the data.

Risk is monitored, not merely catalogued. A Project Steering Group meets at five points - M6, M14, M18, M24 and M27 - and issues a go/no-go verdict on milestones MS1-MS5; the four scheduled verdict points coincide with the milestone months so that no work package advances past a failed gate, and the retained M27 point provides a mid-placement review so the evaluated M25-M30 placement never runs unmonitored. The Career Development Plan is reviewed at the same five points. Administrative risks are handled through the same governance: the written field-access arrangement with the commercial farmer (T3.1), the MATE data-use conditions, the ELTE instrument-access schedule and the placement arrangement with AgroVIR are all being confirmed in writing before the action starts, and until they are they are carried as declared assumptions rather than as settled fact, so the plan is transparent about what remains to be closed at grant preparation.

### Gantt chart (months elapsed)

The chart below shows the work packages, major deliverables (D), milestones (MS) and the M25-M30 non-academic placement against elapsed project months 1-30. There is no secondment (European Fellowship); the placement is the mobility element shown on WP5.

```
                              1         2         3
Month (elapsed):    123456789012345678901234567890
                    ------------------------------
WP1  Data/stress    ######........................
WP2  Modelling      ..############................
WP3  Field valid.   ...###############............
WP4  DrR MVP        ########################......
WP5  Placement      ........................######
                    ------------------------------
Markers:            ..^..^.......^...^.....^.....^
                    ------------------------------
  M3  : D1.3 (Career Development Plan)
  M6  : D1.1, D1.2  | MS1 Historical knowledge base and target definition complete
  M14 : D2.1, D2.2  | MS2 Model and scale-transition framework ready for final prospective assessment
  M18 : D3.1, D3.2  | MS3 Independent real-world transferability quantified
  M24 : D4.1, D4.2  | MS4 MVP ready for industrial placement evaluation
  M30 : D5.1, D5.2  | MS5 Industrial evaluation and placement completed

Placement (non-academic, AgroVIR): M25-M30, mainly remote with monthly
  face-to-face technical reviews (WP5).
Critical path: T1.3 -> T2.2 -> T3.5 -> T4.3 -> T5.1.
```

The Gantt is included within the 10-page limit for Part B Sections 1-3 and shows months elapsed rather than calendar dates, as required. It makes the plan's logic legible at a glance: an early knowledge-base and training gate (M6), a modelling gate (M14), the decisive independent-validation gate (M18), the MVP-ready gate (M24) that admits the placement, and the closing industrial-evaluation gate (M30).

claim_statuses.claim_summary: The work plan comprises five work packages (WP1 Data Harmonisation and Physiological Stress Definition; WP2 HUN-REN Modelling and ELTE Scale Harmonisation; WP3 Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation; WP4 DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation; WP5 AgroVIR Non-Academic Placement), single-beneficiary at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont.
Eleven deliverables D1.1-D5.2 with the stated due months (D1.3 M3; D1.1/D1.2 M6; D2.1/D2.2 M14; D3.1/D3.2 M18; D4.1/D4.2 M24; D5.1/D5.2 M30).
Five milestones MS1 (M6), MS2 (M14), MS3 (M18), MS4 (M24), MS5 (M30) with verifiable criteria and titles as stated.

WP leads: HOST (HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont) leads WP1 and WP2; the validation site leads WP3; КРУМАТИК ЕООД leads WP4; AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság leads WP5.
European Fellowship of 30 months at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (M1-M24) plus a six-month non-academic placement at AgroVIR (M25-M30); no separate secondment.
Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is the fellow; primary supervisor Dr. Roland Hollós (ATK); co-supervisor Prof. András Jung (associated partner ELTE).
Inter-WP dependencies (WP1->WP2/WP3, WP2->WP3/WP4, WP3->WP4, WP4->WP5 finish-to-start) and critical path T1.3->T2.2->T3.5->T4.3->T5.1; graph acyclic.
Schedule places WP1 M1-6, WP2 M3-14, WP3 M4-18, WP4 M1-24, WP5 M25-30, all within the 30-month duration; strict finish-to-start couplings honoured with slack.
Fellow's 30 person-months split WP1 3.0, WP2 6.0, WP3 6.6, WP4 6.0, WP5 5.4, cross-cutting 3.0.
Ten-row risk register R01-R10 with likelihood, impact and mitigation covering research and administrative risks.
Risk philosophy: prospective performance loss is treated as a quantified scientific result with limited transparent recalibration rather than hidden.
Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route is a contingency for loss of primary farmer-site access (R04, task T3.6).
Project Steering Group meets at M6, M14, M18, M24 and M27, issuing go/no-go verdicts on MS1-MS5, with the M27 point a mid-placement review; CDP reviewed at the same five points.

The M25-M30 placement is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment. The fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment; AgroVIR provides the information and data extracts required for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers, e.g. 'Field X'). The fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.

The independent commercial farmer provides written field access: site availability for the validation season(s) within M4-M18, permission for sensor installation (automated meteorological station, soil sensors), field measurements and UAV campaigns, agreed irrigation-treatment implementation, and routine crop management responsibilities.

The fellow conducts or co-conducts UAV and hyperspectral measurements with ELTE's DJI Matrice 350 RTK platform (Zenmuse L1/P1/H20T) and Ultris S5 / Cubert CUVIS cameras, supported by Dr. Zsófia Varga for flight planning, sensor operation and data acquisition, scheduled around key physiological measurement dates at the validation site; ELTE software environments are available for processing.
Career Development Plan is deliverable D1.3, due M3, and is reviewed at each steering point.
